_comment: Single source of truth for every project on the site. Edit here, or through admin.html, then run: node build/build.js . Order in this list is the order on the page. published:false keeps a project on file but off the site entirely. Empty fields and empty arrays are simply not rendered, so nothing half-written ever ships.

projects.title: Asmi
projects.subtitle: Brand identity for an apparel brand
projects.summary: A culturally inspired apparel brand built around one idea: that clothing can be a way of wearing your identity. Audience, positioning and personality first, then the logo system, type, palette and surface patterns.
projects.decision:
Dummy text. This is the decision the page is named after. The audience you found, the position nobody else was holding, or the thing the founder had been saying for years without realising it was the whole brand.

State it plainly, then say what followed from it. Every colour, every typeface and every packaging choice should trace back to this paragraph. That is the difference between work that holds and work that gets replaced in two years.
projects.brief:
Dummy text. This is where the brief goes. Who came to you, what stage the business was at, and what was getting in their way. Keep it concrete, because the reader is deciding whether their own problem sounds like this one.

A second paragraph sits here when the story needs one. A blank line in the editor becomes a new paragraph on the page, so you can write at whatever length the project deserves.
projects.outcome: Dummy text. What changed once the work landed. Ideally what the brand could then charge, or who it could then talk to that it could not reach before. A number is better than an adjective, and a client sentence is better than both.
